Console.set_window_title mirrors the existing show_cursor pattern (base rich/console.py:1143-1152: `if self.is_terminal: self.control(...); return True; return False`).

The Windows path extends the existing legacy_windows_render dispatch chain rather than adding a new renderer.
Test additions follow the existing renderer test pattern (legacy_term_mock + assert_called_once_with).
Console.set_window_title never emits raw escape text; it goes through Control.title (rich/console.py:1166), so framing stays in control.py:33.
The Windows renderer uses the LegacyWindowsTerm facade (term.set_title) and does not call Win32 APIs directly (rich/_windows_renderer.py:56).
Tests use create_autospec(LegacyWindowsTerm) (tests/test_windows_renderer.py:12-14) rather than touching the console API.
Docstrings use the repo's Google style (Args:/Returns: sections) as in control.py move() and console.py show_cursor.

Minor, not a violation: the set_window_title docstring (console.py:1155-1168) is shorter than the reference's, omitting the caveats about persistence and unsupported terminals. Its first line still states that Rich cannot restore titles.

Behavior: on a terminal, Console.set_window_title writes OSC 0 (`\x1b]0;<title>\x07`) through the normal control path (rich/console.py:1165-1168, rich/control.py:33), and returns False when not a terminal. This matches the reference.
Legacy Windows consoles receive the title via LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title (rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56), matching the reference.
_render_buffer (rich/console.py:1989-2006) emits control text for terminal output, so the sequence reaches the terminal in the non-legacy path.
Reference-only items (the __main__ demo in control.py, reordering in test_live.py, the CHANGELOG reshuffle) are not behavioral requirements, so their absence is not a failure.
